item.title: 3 things to know about naval blockades as U.S. begins patrols in the Strait of Hormuz
item.summary: The White House says it wants to choke off Iran's oil export revenue. But experts say that blockades are often unpredictable and difficult to enforce.

item.title: Russian missiles and drones bombard Ukraine in hourslong attack
item.summary: Russia hammered civilian areas of Ukraine with hundreds of drones and dozens of missiles in an attack that stretched for hours killing at least 16 people.

item.title: Middle East conflict causes a fluoride shortage for US drinking water
item.summary: Some U.S. water systems are cutting back on fluoride because of a key chemical is in short supply. Israel is one of its main producers.

item.title: Jury finds that Live Nation acted as a monopoly and overcharged ticket buyers
item.summary: An antitrust suit alleged that the company unfairly controlled too much of the live music industry at the expense of venues, artists and fans. The decision could reshape the industry.

item.title: Whiting Foundation names its 10 emerging authors of 2026
item.summary: The annual Whiting Award for Emerging Writers comes with $50,000 to support each winner's work. It's one of the largest prizes granted to promising new authors.

item.title: Popes have spoken out on politics before. But with Trump and Pope Leo it's different
item.summary: President Trump's attacks on Pope Leo are unprecedented, religious experts told NPR. Here's how the situation differs from other popes' political critiques.

item.title: French government seeking release of 86-year-old French widow detained by ICE
item.summary: The French government is pressing the U.S. Department of Homeland Security to release the 86-year-old French widow of a military veteran from immigration custody in Louisiana after she was detained earlier this month.

item.title: Bukele signs reforms allowing life prison sentences for people as young as 12
item.summary: The reforms signed by Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele would apply to people convicted of committing or being an accomplice to crimes including homicide, femicide, rape and gang membership.

item.title: What Orban's loss means for far right movements around the world
item.summary: The defeat of Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban at the polls is fueling questions about what's in store for far-right movements in other countries that exploit extremist conspiracies to win.

item.title: A Colorado hospital profits from resolving language barriers
item.summary: Without qualified interpreters at doctors' offices, non-English speakers can face bad — even fatal — health outcomes. A hospital in rural Colorado is training its existing bilingual staff to address the service gap.
